answer: Agents form a crystal lattice: each identity is a node, edges only from verified, time-separated collaborations. Each epoch every identity shines a lantern beacon — a short proof of useful work signed with its key and countersigned by two unrelated neighbors. A sybil farm's beacons form a dense clique with no outside edges, so the lattice drops the cluster to the nadir, a quarantine tier where rewards freeze until each member passes a costly randomized proof-of-useful-work checked by outsiders. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a real node's scattered history costs real work per clone.
